A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSSD research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original experiments measuring token acceptance, retrieval time, latency and throughput across models, tasks and languages.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds retrieval-cost measurements across datastore sizes and CPU architectures in Figure 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects its match test from i = |prefix| to i = |p|, allowing matching shorter prefixes to be returned. This locally changes the documented procedure; fusion weights and the speculation-length rule remain unchanged. The expanded datastore-management description does not establish an underlying implementation change.

E1.justification: MT-Bench and its translations, GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, SWE-Bench and PG-19 remain the evaluated datasets and tasks. Languages and data sources are retained. The added timing study varies datastore capacity and host configurations.

E2.justification: Matching experiments retain the same comparator membership, including their differing subsets of PLD, REST, Lookahead, EAGLE-2, EAGLE-3, Llama-3.2-1B drafting and autoregressive decoding. The new retrieval-cost study adds no competing method.

E3.justification: Figure 2 introduces a timing protocol with 16 candidates, batch sizes 1–64 and two CPU architectures. Existing captions revise GPU specifications. The large-model caption changes one GPU per prefill/decode stage to two, agreeing with the TP=2 prose already present in v2. These reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Figure 2 tests how retrieval cost scales with datastore size and batch size on x86-64 and aarch64 hosts. This adds targeted scalability and hardware-sensitivity evidence. Existing component ablations, cold-start experiments and distribution-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages for the multilingual cold-start and reasoning experiments. v3 adds no run-count revisions, seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests; the new timing curves continue mean-only reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds retrieval timings across datastores from 100 kB to 57 GB, showing increasing cost across the tested configurations. All previously published plotted series are retained. Table 1 also retains its values, including SSSD speedups of 1.23× and 1.26×.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds O(P log N) search-cost analysis. Table 2 revises byte accounting, tensor-parallel shapes and approximation conditions. Appendix B changes the Q-intensity denominator from 2/h + 1/(b*s_q) to 1/h + 1/(b*s_q); the latter disagrees with Table 2 at p=1. These are localized mathematical additions and revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: training-free speculation, easier deployment, hardware-aware scaling, robustness across languages and domains, and acceleration up to 2.9×. Contribution-list rewriting does not expand those claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly connects multilingual speedups to tokenization disparities and hypothesizes language-specific/tokenizer effects, leaving systematic investigation to future work. Ethical considerations removes the suggestion that per-user datastores could aid privacy compliance and performance. The main MoE, MLA and host-resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands operational documentation: 512M-token subindices, approximately 4 GB each, an eight-index cap, shared sampling, asynchronous rebuilding and memory pooling. It newly specifies 14 GB and 18 GB experimental datastores and CPU configurations. It also replaces the future code-release promise with a source-code availability statement and repository address.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ahia et al. (2023) and Petrov et al. (2023) to position multilingual gains against tokenizer disparities. The speculative-decoding literature discussion remains substantively stable. Updated Llama authorship and removal of a duplicate Chen reference concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: v3 polishes terminology, capitalization and contribution wording, adds a datastore-management subsection, and organizes Appendix A into three subsections. These are localized explanatory and structural refinements; the overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, adds the retrieval-cost Figure 2, expands Table 2's caption and revises its labels and equation layout. Hardware captions are edited, and subsequent figures are renumbered. Existing benchmark plots retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The datastore documentation, code-access information and new scalability measurements make v3 easier to reproduce and assess. Algorithm 1 and GPU-count corrections also improve clarity. These benefits outweigh a localized new inconsistency between Appendix B's Q-intensity equation and Table 2, but the unchanged principal benchmark evidence limits the overall gain.
